questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):
1. It is conducted by the National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
2. It replaced the Labour Bureau's Quarterly Employment Survey as the main source of labour force data.
3. It provides quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for urban areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PLFS is run by the NSO (MoSPI) and gives quarterly urban estimates plus annual all-India estimates. It replaced the NSSO's older quinquennial employment-unemployment surveys, not the Labour Bureau's Quarterly Employment Survey, which still runs separately.
questions.s: MoSPI/NSO PLFS reports; Ramesh Singh, Unemployment chapter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reference periods used in labour force surveys:
1. Usual principal status is decided by the activity on which a person spent the longer time during the 365 days preceding the survey.
2. A person who worked for at least 30 days in some other economic activity during the 365 days is said to have a subsidiary status activity.
3. Current weekly status uses a reference period of the preceding 30 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Principal status uses the major time criterion over 365 days and subsidiary status needs 30 days or more of other work. Current weekly status uses the preceding 7 days, not 30.
questions.s: MoSPI, PLFS concepts and definitions; Ramesh Singh
questions.h: Year for principal, week for CWS, 30 days for subsidiary.

questions.q: In the Periodic Labour Force Survey, which one of the following persons is classified as 'employed'?
o: A person helping without pay in a household farm or enterprise
A full-time student preparing for a competitive examination
A retired pensioner who is neither working nor seeking work
A person engaged only in domestic duties for her own household
questions.e: PLFS counts unpaid helpers in a household enterprise as self-employed, so they are employed even without a wage. Students, pensioners and persons doing only own-household domestic duties fall outside the labour force.

questions.q: In a region, the population is 1,000, the labour force is 400 and 360 of the labour force are employed. Which one of the following gives the labour force participation rate, worker population ratio and unemployment rate respectively?
questions.e: LFPR = 400/1000 = 40 percent and WPR = 360/1000 = 36 percent. The unemployment rate divides the 40 unemployed by the labour force of 400, giving 10 percent, not by population (4) or by the employed (about 11).
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Unemployment chapter; PLFS definitions
questions.h: Unemployment rate always sits on the labour force.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Type of unemployment : Example
1. Frictional : A graduate who quits one job and spends some weeks searching for a better one
2. Cyclical : Layoffs across industries during a recession caused by a fall in aggregate demand
3. Seasonal : Workers whose skills became obsolete after a new technology replaced their trade
4. Disguised : Workers laid off when a firm shuts down a loss-making unit
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Skill obsolescence from new technology is structural or technological unemployment, not seasonal, and disguised unemployment means surplus workers whose marginal productivity is near zero, not laid-off workers.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Disguised unemployment is mostly found in the agricultural sector of India.
Statement-II: Seasonal unemployment occurs in agriculture because farm operations are tied to specific parts of the crop calendar.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true but about different things. Disguised unemployment is surplus labour on small farms with near-zero marginal productivity, while seasonal unemployment is idleness in the off-season, so one does not explain the other.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four labour codes enacted by Parliament in 2019-2020?
questions.e: The four codes are Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions. The factory law is folded into the OSH Code; there is no separate Factories and Welfare Code.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Industrial Relations Code, 2020:
1. Prior government permission for lay-off, retrenchment and closure is required in establishments with at least 300 workers.
2. A notice of 14 days is required before a strike in all industrial establishments.
3. Fixed-term employment is not recognised under the Code.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Code raised the permission threshold from 100 to 300 workers and extended the 14-day strike notice from public utility services to all establishments. It explicitly recognises fixed-term employment, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Code on Wages, 2019:
1. It subsumes the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976.
2. The Central Government fixes a floor wage, and wages fixed by States cannot be below it.
3. It subsumes the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Wages Code merges four laws: Payment of Wages, Minimum Wages, Payment of Bonus and Equal Remuneration. The provident fund law goes into the Code on Social Security, not into the Wages Code.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Code on Social Security, 2020:
1. It formally defines 'gig worker' and 'platform worker'.
2. Aggregators must contribute 10 percent of their annual turnover to a social security fund for gig workers.
3. The Central Government may frame schemes for gig and platform workers covering benefits such as life and disability cover.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Code gives legal definitions and empowers schemes for gig and platform workers. The aggregator contribution is 1 to 2 percent of annual turnover, capped at 5 percent of the amount paid to such workers, not 10 percent.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: According to the NITI Aayog report on India's gig and platform economy released in 2022, the number of gig workers was estimated at about 7.7 million in 2020-21 and is projected to reach about how many by 2029-30?
questions.e: The report estimated gig workers at 7.7 million in 2020-21, rising to 23.5 million by 2029-30. The projection implies roughly three times growth in a decade.
questions.s: NITI Aayog, India's Booming Gig and Platform Economy, June 2022

questions.q: Which one of the following States was the first to enact a law for the registration and welfare of platform-based gig workers?
questions.e: Rajasthan enacted the Rajasthan Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration and Welfare) Act in 2023, the first such State law. Karnataka and some other States followed later.
questions.s: The Hindu / PIB reporting, 2023; Ramesh Singh

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 as originally enacted:
1. It provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.
2. The Centre bears the entire wage cost of unskilled labour.
3. Contractors and labour-displacing machinery may be used at the discretion of the Gram Panchayat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act is demand-driven with a legal guarantee, and the Centre pays all unskilled wage cost. Contractors and labour-displacing machinery are prohibited, so that employment goes directly to workers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the MGNREGA, 2005 as originally enacted:
1. Wages are to be paid on a weekly basis and not later than a fortnight.
2. If work is not provided within 15 days of demand, an unemployment allowance is payable by the State Government.
3. Work is to be provided within 5 km of the applicant's residence, failing which extra wages are payable.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are statutory provisions: wage payment within a fortnight, a State-paid unemployment allowance after 15 days of unmet demand, and a 5 km norm with 10 percent extra wages beyond it. These make the employment right enforceable.

questions.q:
With reference to the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA, 2005 as originally enacted, consider the following statements:
1. At least one-third of the beneficiaries are to be women.
2. Social audit of works by the Gram Sabha is mandatory.
3. The scheme was launched in all districts of the country simultaneously in 2006.
4. A wage to material cost ratio of 60:40 is to be maintained.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The scheme was phased in: 200 districts in 2006, then more in 2007, and all rural districts by 2008.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Scheme) with List-II (Purpose):
List-I
A. DDU-GKY
B. NAPS
C. PM SVANidhi
D. Stand-Up India
List-II
1. Placement-linked skilling of rural youth
2. Sharing of apprentices' stipend with employers
3. Working capital loans for street vendors
4. Bank loans for greenfield enterprises of SC/ST and women entrepreneurs
questions.e: DDU-GKY is the rural placement-linked skilling programme, NAPS shares the apprentice stipend cost with employers, SVANidhi gives collateral-free working capital to street vendors and Stand-Up India supports SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

questions.q: The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) was set up as a public-private partnership company in which the Government of India holds
questions.e: NSDC is a not-for-profit company with 49 percent government and 51 percent private sector shareholding. The private majority was meant to push industry-led skill training.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF):
1. It organises qualifications into levels from 1 to 5.
2. The levels are graded according to knowledge, skills and aptitude.
3. Recognition of Prior Learning allows skills acquired informally to be certified.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NSQF has ten levels, from 1 to 10, graded by knowledge, skills and aptitude. RPL is the route that certifies experience gained outside formal education.

questions.q: The Skill India Mission was launched on the occasion of
questions.e: The Skill India Mission and the National Policy for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship 2015 were launched on 15 July 2015, the UN-designated World Youth Skills Day.

questions.q:
Which of the following skill development initiatives in India are supported by World Bank assistance?
1. SANKALP
2. STRIVE
3. PMKVY
4. DDU-GKY
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: SANKALP (state skill governance) and STRIVE (ITIs and apprenticeships) are World Bank-assisted. PMKVY and DDU-GKY are funded from the Union Budget.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the PM Vishwakarma scheme:
1. It targets only urban street vendors.
2. Beneficiaries receive a training stipend of Rs 500 per month.
3. Beneficiaries receive a toolkit incentive of Rs 50,000.
4. It was launched in September 2023 for traditional artisans and craftspeople.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 4 is correct. The scheme covers rural and urban artisans, with a stipend of Rs 500 per day and a toolkit incentive of Rs 15,000.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana loans are refinanced through MUDRA, which is a subsidiary of
questions.e: MUDRA was set up in 2015 as a wholly owned subsidiary of SIDBI, the apex bank for MSMEs. It refinances lending institutions rather than lending directly, in the Shishu, Kishor and Tarun categories.

questions.q: Stand-Up India scheme facilitates bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore, with each bank branch lending to at least one SC/ST borrower and one woman borrower, for
o: setting up greenfield enterprises in manufacturing, services or trading
expanding existing enterprises of any entrepreneur
agricultural crop production by small farmers
consumption needs of urban slum households
questions.e: The scheme was launched in 2016 for first-time entrepreneurs from SC/ST and women, with loans meant for new greenfield enterprises. It is not a crop-loan or consumption-loan product.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the e-Shram portal:
1. It is a national database of unorganised workers linked with Aadhaar.
2. Income tax payers can also register on it.
3. Workers aged 16 to 59 years who are not members of EPFO or ESIC are eligible.
4. Registered workers get a 12-digit Universal Account Number.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Income tax payers are excluded from e-Shram registration, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment, 2021

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan scheme for unorganised workers, the assured minimum monthly pension after the age of 60 is
questions.e: PM-SYM promises Rs 3,000 a month after 60 to unorganised workers aged 18 to 40 with monthly income up to Rs 15,000. Atal Pension Yojana is the one with a Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 range.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: If an economy's output grows by 8 percent in a year while employment grows by 2 percent, the employment elasticity of output is
questions.e: Employment elasticity = percentage change in employment divided by percentage change in output = 2/8 = 0.25. A low value like this is the arithmetic behind 'jobless growth'.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Female labour force participation in India tends to fall as household incomes rise from low levels.
Statement-II: Higher household income reduces the compulsion on women to take up low-paid, arduous work, and social norms often discourage their paid work outside the home.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: This is the downward arm of the U-shaped relation between development and women's participation. The income effect plus social norms explain why women withdraw from distress work when household income rises.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Unemployment chapter (U-shaped hypothesis of Claudia Goldin)
questions.h: Income up, distress work down: the U-curve dip.

questions.q:
Which of the following Acts are subsumed in the Code on Social Security, 2020?
1. Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
2. Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948
3. Payment of Bonus Act, 1965
4. Maternity Benefit Act, 1961
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Social Security Code absorbs nine laws including the EPF Act, ESI Act and Maternity Benefit Act. The Payment of Bonus Act is subsumed in the Code on Wages, not here.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q:
Statement-I: The unemployment rate measured by Current Weekly Status is generally higher than that measured by Usual Status in India.
Statement-II: Current Weekly Status uses a reference period of the preceding 365 days.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The short seven-day window catches intermittent spells without work, so the weekly-status rate runs higher than the usual-status rate. But that reference period is the preceding 7 days, not 365.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, minimum wage provisions apply only to employments listed in a Schedule.
Statement-II: The Code on Wages applies to all employees in both organised and unorganised sectors.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The old Minimum Wages Act worked through scheduled employments, which left many workers out. The Code removes that limit and covers all employees, so Statement-I describes the old position.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, trade unions, industrial and labour disputes, and social security and social insurance are subjects in the
o: Union List for central employees and State List for others
questions.e: Labour matters are in the Concurrent List, which is why Parliament can pass labour codes while States can also legislate and amend them. Hence the Centre's codes need State rules to be operational.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Article of the Constitution) with List-II (Directive Principle):
List-I
A. Article 41
B. Article 42
C. Article 43
D. Article 43A
List-II
1. Participation of workers in the management of industries
2. Living wage and decent standard of life for workers
3. Just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief
4. Right to work, education and public assistance in certain cases
questions.e: Article 41 is work, education and public assistance, 42 is just conditions and maternity relief, 43 is living wage and 43A (added by the 42nd Amendment) is workers' participation in management.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment?
questions.e: Article 24, a Fundamental Right against exploitation, bans child employment in hazardous work. Article 23 bans trafficking and forced labour, and Article 21A is about free and compulsory education.

questions.q: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, which defined the informal sector and estimated the poor and vulnerable among informal workers, was chaired by
questions.e: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under Arjun Sengupta and its 2007 report highlighted that most informal workers lived at low consumption levels. Rangarajan and Tendulkar are associated with poverty-line committees.

questions.q: The development model based on the idea of an 'unlimited supply of labour' moving from subsistence agriculture to the modern industrial sector at a constant wage is associated with
questions.e: Lewis argued that surplus labour in agriculture lets industry expand without raising wages until the surplus is exhausted. Kuznets is known for the inequality curve and Nurkse for the vicious circle of poverty.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Economic Growth and Development chapter

questions.q: The India Employment Report 2024 was jointly released by the International Labour Organization and the
questions.e: The report, released in March 2024, was a collaboration between the ILO and the Institute for Human Development, New Delhi. It drew attention to youth unemployment and educated joblessness.
questions.s: ILO and IHD, India Employment Report 2024

questions.q:
Which of the following price indices are compiled by the Labour Bureau?
1. Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers
2. Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers
3. Consumer Price Index (Combined)
4. Wholesale Price Index
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Labour Bureau compiles CPI-IW, CPI-AL and CPI-RL. The headline CPI (Combined) comes from the NSO, and the WPI from the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.
questions.s: Labour Bureau; Ramesh Singh, Inflation chapter

questions.q: Under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme, the Central Government shares what proportion of the prescribed stipend with employers, subject to a monthly cap?
questions.e: NAPS, launched in 2016, reimburses 25 percent of the stipend (up to a ceiling) to encourage employers to take on apprentices. Employers bear the rest.

questions.q: The Deendayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) is a placement-linked skill programme of the
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
questions.e: DDU-GKY targets rural youth aged 15 to 35 and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission. MSDE runs PMKVY and the ITI network.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET):
1. It was constituted in 2018 by merging the National Council for Vocational Training and the National Skill Development Agency.
2. It regulates awarding bodies and assessment agencies in vocational education.
3. It functions under the Ministry of Education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NCVET is the single regulator formed to merge two overlapping skill bodies. It works under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, not the Ministry of Education.

questions.q: The idea of a guaranteed-work rural programme that influenced the MGNREGA is most closely linked to the earlier employment guarantee scheme of
questions.e: Maharashtra's Employment Guarantee Scheme, backed by the 1977 Act and financed by its own taxes, was the model for a legal guarantee of work. MGNREGA took this idea to the national level.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rural employment programmes in the chronological order of their launch:
1. Sampoorna Grameen Rozgar Yojana
2. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana
3. Employment Assurance Scheme
4. National Rural Employment Guarantee Act
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The order is JRY (1989), EAS (1993), SGRY (2001) and then NREGA (2005). SGRY was later merged into the NREGA.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Poverty Alleviation and Employment Programmes
questions.h: JRY, EAS, SGRY, then the Act.

questions.q: Which type of unemployment is most likely to result when rapid automation makes an existing set of skills obsolete in an industry?
questions.e: Here the demand for particular skills falls permanently while the workers' skills do not match new jobs, which is structural. Cyclical unemployment comes from deficient aggregate demand, and frictional from job search.

questions.q:
In the labour force surveys of India, which of the following are outside the labour force?
1. A full-time student who is neither working nor seeking work
2. A person engaged only in domestic duties for her own household
3. A person who did not work but was available for work and seeking it
4. An unpaid helper in a family business
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The labour force is the employed plus the unemployed (seeking or available for work). Students and those engaged only in own-household domestic duties are outside it, while unpaid family helpers are employed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Quarterly Employment Survey (QES):
1. It is conducted by the Labour Bureau.
2. It covers establishments with 10 or more workers in selected non-farm sectors.
3. It is the source of rural labour force estimates in the PLFS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: QES is an establishment survey of the Labour Bureau that tracks organised employment. PLFS is a household survey by the NSO, so QES does not feed its rural estimates.
questions.s: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q:
Match List-I (Labour Code) with List-II (An Act subsumed by it):
List-I
A. Code on Wages
B. Industrial Relations Code
C. Code on Social Security
D. Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code
List-II
1. Minimum Wages Act, 1948
2. Trade Unions Act, 1926
3. Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948
4. Factories Act, 1948
questions.e: Each code merges older laws by theme: pay (Minimum Wages Act), industrial relations (Trade Unions Act), social security (ESI Act) and workplace safety (Factories Act).
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: The PM SVANidhi scheme, launched in 2020 under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, mainly provides
o: housing loans to the urban poor
collateral-free working capital loans to street vendors
subsidised raw material to traditional artisans
crop loans to small and marginal farmers
questions.e: SVANidhi was designed as a post-lockdown relief to restore the livelihoods of street vendors through small, collateral-free loans with interest subsidy for timely repayment.

questions.q: The National Career Service portal, which links jobseekers, employers and training providers, is an initiative of the
o: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.e: NCS was launched in 2015 as a digital job-matching platform and is run by the Ministry of Labour and Employment. MSDE focuses on training through Skill India.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 is correct?
o: It applies to establishments employing 20 or more contract workers
It subsumes the Minimum Wages Act, 1948
It excludes inter-State migrant workers from its scope
Women may work at night in all establishments with their consent and prescribed safeguards
questions.e: The OSH Code permits night work by women with consent and safeguards. The contract labour threshold is 50, minimum wages are in the Wages Code, and inter-State migrant workers are covered.
questions.s: PIB, Ministry of Labour and Employment

questions.q: The 'natural rate of unemployment' in an economy refers to the rate at which
o: every person willing to work at any wage is employed
unemployment is entirely voluntary and involves no job search
only frictional and structural unemployment remain and cyclical unemployment is absent
the economy is operating below potential output
questions.e: At the natural rate the economy is at full employment in the macro sense: people are still between jobs or mismatched, but there is no deficiency of demand. Output is then at its potential level.
